title: Software Testing Quiz
description: Revisit the key ideas in Software Testing. Read each choice carefully. You can try the quiz again after reviewing the lessons.

questions.question: What does true tell us here?
questions.explanation: A test compares an expected result with the actual result. A passing test only checks the case you gave it. The result is true: the actual answer matches 5. This does not prove every possible input works.

questions.question: Which pair covers both free and paid entry?
questions.explanation: A test case includes inputs and the expected result. Choose cases that exercise different rules. The output is true false. The examples cover both sides of the age rule.

questions.question: Which age is exactly on the boundary?
questions.explanation: A boundary is where a rule changes. Values just before, on and after it are especially useful tests. The output is false true true. Age 10 is allowed because the rule includes equality.

questions.question: What result does the empty list produce?
questions.explanation: An empty list has no items. Decide what your program should do with it before writing a test. The result is 0. The starting value lets reduce handle an empty array.

questions.question: What does a negative test check?
options: Only negative numbers in every program
questions.explanation: A negative test checks how a program rejects an invalid input. The expected result may be a useful error instead of a normal value. The output explains that a negative side is not allowed. Rejecting it is the expected behaviour.

questions.question: Which test checks parts working together?
questions.explanation: A unit test checks a small part. An integration test checks parts working together. Each finds different mistakes. The tests grow from one calculation to a whole visible journey.

questions.question: Which detail helps someone reproduce a bug?
questions.explanation: A bug report should let another person repeat the problem. Include steps, expected behaviour and actual behaviour. These details give someone a clear starting point. Personal details are not needed.

questions.question: Why keep a regression test?
options: To catch the same problem returning
questions.explanation: A regression happens when something that worked stops working. Add a test for a fixed bug so later changes check it again. The test records the behaviour that should stay fixed.

questions.question: What makes this test repeatable?
options: It uses the current time secretly
questions.explanation: A repeatable test gives the same result with the same inputs. Pass changing values in instead of hiding the current time in the calculation. The result is always true for these inputs. The test does not depend on today's real date.

questions.question: What guides exploratory testing?
questions.explanation: Exploratory testing uses a goal and careful observation. You choose the next step from what you discover. The exploration has a clear purpose and written observations.

questions.question: What should a keyboard user be able to see?
questions.explanation: Accessibility means people with different needs can use the app. Test labels, keyboard access and visible focus as well as mouse clicks. A learner can understand and operate the search without a mouse. Automatic checks help, but people still need to review it.

questions.question: What belongs in a test summary?
options: Uncovered areas as well as results
questions.explanation: A test summary says what ran, what passed and what remains unchecked. It should not promise more than the evidence supports. The summary tells others both the useful evidence and its limits.
